title_or_table: Poverty in the United States: 2025 (P60-290), Table 8, Number and Percentage of People in Poverty Using the Supplemental Poverty Measure by Age, Race, and Hispanic Origin: 2009 to 2025; and Table 3, Poverty Status of People by Age, Race, and Hispanic Origin Using the Official Poverty Measure: 1959 to 2025
table_id: P60-290 Table 8 (SPM); P60-290 Table 3 (official measure); P60-287 Table B-2 (earlier SPM vintage)
universe_or_base: People covered by the Current Population Survey Annual Social and Economic Supplement (CPS ASEC); the table notes 'Population as of March of the following year.' age_group under_18 is people under 18 years; all_ages is all people
unit: percent is the share of the age group below the poverty line; moe_pct is the 90 percent margin of error in percentage points; counts are in thousands
vintage: Default vintage p60-290, released September 15, 2026. Its 2019 to 2024 SPM values use the corrected 2026 threshold method (BLS correction of July 17, 2026; Census working paper SEHSD WP2026-17, August 19, 2026), and every 2024 value uses Vintage 2025 population controls. Rows with vintage p60-287 (released September 9, 2025) keep the earlier SPM series for comparison; they hold the values as first published for 2020, 2021 and 2024
qualification: SPM estimates for 2019 to 2024 were revised in August 2026 after a correction to the poverty thresholds; values here differ from those first published by -0.4 to +0.1 percentage points. A change between two years is a descriptive change, not the effect of one policy

measure.description: spm (Supplemental Poverty Measure) or official (official poverty measure)

series_variant.description: standard, or which of two estimates the table gives for a break year (2013, 2017, 2019)

comparable_with.description: for break years: later means use with the years after, earlier with the years before; both otherwise

moe_pct.description: 90 percent margin of error, percentage points (SPM only)

moe_thousands.description: 90 percent margin of error, thousands (SPM only)

population_thousands.description: people in the age group, thousands

note.description: Census footnote text or a description of the break

printed_source_line: Source: U.S. Census Bureau, Poverty in the United States: 2025 (P60-290), Table 8, Supplemental Poverty Measure, children under 18, 2009 to 2025, United States. Retrieved November 6, 2026. Figures for 2019 to 2024 include the Bureau’s August 2026 correction to the poverty thresholds, and 2024 also takes new population weights; they differ by up to 0.4 points from the earlier release.

source_line_variants.source_line_official_measure: Source: U.S. Census Bureau, Poverty in the United States: 2025 (P60-290), Table 3, official poverty measure, children under 18, 2009 to 2025, United States. Retrieved November 6, 2026. The official measure compares pretax money income with a national threshold and leaves out several assistance programs that the SPM counts.
source_line_variants.source_line_first_published: Source: U.S. Census Bureau, Poverty in the United States: 2024 (P60-287), Table B-2, Supplemental Poverty Measure, children under 18, 2020, 2021 and 2024, United States. Retrieved November 6, 2026. Rates as published before the Bureau’s August 2026 correction; P60-277 (September 13, 2022) printed the same 2020 and 2021 rates.
source_line_variants.source_line_both_measures: Source: U.S. Census Bureau, Poverty in the United States: 2025 (P60-290), Table 8, Supplemental Poverty Measure, and Table 3, official poverty measure, children under 18, 2009 to 2025, United States. Retrieved November 6, 2026. Figures for 2019 to 2024 include the Bureau’s August 2026 correction to the poverty thresholds, and 2024 also takes new population weights; they differ by up to 0.4 points from the earlier release.

which_vintage_to_chart: Use vintage p60-290 for any chart of the series. Use a p60-287 value only when a chart quotes a figure as first published, and say so in the source line

v7_comparison.v7_figures: Atlas V7 numbers[5]: 9.7% (2020), 5.2% (2021), 13.4% (2024), labeled 'as first published'
v7_comparison.first_published_match: Yes. P60-287 Table B-2 gives under-18 SPM rates of 9.7 (2020), 5.2 (2021) and 13.4 (2024); P60-277 Table B-2 (September 13, 2022) also gives 9.7 (2020) and 5.2 (2021)
v7_comparison.why_they_differ: 2020 and 2021 fell 0.1 point under the corrected thresholds (working paper Table 4). 2024 is 13.4 under the corrected thresholds with Vintage 2024 controls (working paper Table 4) and 13.5 after P60-290 reweighted 2024 to Vintage 2025 population controls (SEHSD WP2026-16 page; P60-290 Table 8 footnote 3)
v7_comparison.w001_note: V7 source W001's note reads 'official child poverty 13.4%, a record low'. P60-290 Table 3 gives the official-measure rate for children in 2025 as 13.4. That is a different measure and year from the SPM 13.4% for 2024 in numbers[5]; keep them apart. The 'record low' wording was not checked

breaks_in_series: 2013: two estimates from split survey panels (redesigned and traditional income questions). 2017: two estimates (updated and earlier processing systems). 2019 (SPM only): two estimates (methodology used from 2019 on, and the original 2011 methodology). Draw a gap or a step at each break, or plot only the comparable_with = later rows for a line that runs to 2025
official_measure_note: The official measure for children sits in Table 3 of the same report, not in the SPM table. Table 3 gives no margins of error, so moe columns are blank for those rows
unconfirmed: The 2020 SPM rate in the original 2020 report (P60-275, September 2021) was not read; the 9.7 figure was read in P60-277 and P60-287
The 'record low' description in V7 source W001 was not checked
